mainTopic: Whether the פר יום הכפורים is a private or communal קרבן, and רבי אלעזר's question about whether a תמורה can take effect on it
overview: The גמרא first tries to prove from רבי אלעזר's question that some תנא holds the פר יום הכפורים is a קרבן ציבור. It rejects the proof: the other view may be that the bull belongs to partners (שותפין). The גמרא then examines רבי אלעזר's question itself: according to the view that the bull is a קרבן יחיד, can a תמורה take effect on it? A first explanation, that the doubt is between the מקדיש and the מתכפר, is rejected as obvious, because תמורה always follows the מתכפר. So the real doubt is whether the fellow כהנים get atonement as an essential part of the bull or only incidentally. The גמרא tries to answer from a ברייתא about a זבח that overrides שבת and טומאה and can make a תמורה, which seems to fit only the bull. רב ששת says the ברייתא could mean the ram of אהרן, and the גמרא supports him, since a bull's substitute (a חטאת's substitute) is left to die. The גמרא answers that 'תמורה' in the ברייתא means substitutes in general, while 'זבח' means a specific offering. It begins to prove this from the strictures of תמורה, and the proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Inferring from רבי אלעזר's question that some say the bull is communal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אלעזר's question about תמורה, which is limited to רבי מאיר's view that the bull is a קרבן יחיד. From that limiting phrase it infers that someone else must hold the bull is a קרבן ציבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says the פר יום הכפורים is a private offering, can a substitution take effect on it or not? Doesn't this imply there is someone who says it is communal?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי אלעזר's question as evidence for the earlier point it was trying to prove. That point is that the פר יום הכפורים might be a קרבן ציבור, which would explain why it stays valid even if the כהן גדול dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר did not just ask about the bull. He asked 'according to the one who says it is a קרבן יחיד.' The גמרא reasons that this qualifier only makes sense if another view exists, and assumes that other view is 'communal.' If so, a communal offering is not disqualified when its owner dies.

keyTerms.meaning: The bull the כהן גדול brings on Yom Kippur
An offering that belongs to a single individual
Trying to swap a consecrated animal for another one; the new animal also becomes holy
Doesn't it follow by implication…?
The community; a communal offering

steps.confusionAlert: A key background fact: a קרבן ציבור (communal offering) cannot be subject to תמורה at all. A private offering can. That is why private versus communal matters so much for this question.

phrases.english: According to the one who says
the Yom Kippur bull is an individual's offering,
does it make a substitution (take effect)
or does it not make a substitution?
Is it not implied
phrases.notes: The גמרא is trying to prove a point from what the words imply.

phrases.english: that there is someone who says it is communal?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו מִכְּלָל דְּאִיכָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר דְּצִבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier question of why the bull is not disqualified when the כהן גדול dies, now offering a proof
steps.raayaObject: That some view holds the פר יום הכפורים is a קרבן ציבור
steps.raayaSupportSource: The limiting wording 'לדברי האומר… קרבן יחיד' in רבי אלעזר's question

steps.title: The other view may be partnership, not communal
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. The view opposing רבי מאיר could be that the bull belongs to partners (the כהן גדול together with his fellow כהנים), not to the whole community.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It implies there is someone who says it belongs to partners.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the inference. The opposing view does not have to be 'communal'; it could be 'partners.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The qualifier in רבי אלעזר's question only proves that some view rejects 'individual.' It does not prove which alternative that view holds, so 'communal' is not proven. Either way, a partnership or a communal offering is not disqualified by the death of one person. So the original question about the כהן גדול dying is still answered.

keyTerms.meaning: Partners; an offering jointly owned by several people (here the כהן גדול and his fellow כהנים)
No; signals a rejection of the proposed proof

steps.whatToRemember: There are three possible categories for the פר: יחיד, שותפין, or ציבור. רבי אלעזר's wording only shows that some view rejects יחיד.

phrases.english: No, it is implied
that there is someone who says it is of partners.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, מִכְּלָל דְּאִיכָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר דְּשׁוּתָּפִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference drawn in step 1
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof that some view holds 'communal'; it leaves standing that some view rejects 'individual'
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The inference assumed the only alternative to 'individual' is 'communal,' ignoring 'partners'

steps.title: Returning to רבי אלעזר's question: what is his doubt?
steps.stepSummary: Using גופא, the גמרא now studies רבי אלעזר's question on its own terms. It asks what makes the case uncertain if the bull is a קרבן יחיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now the matter itself. רבי אלעזר asked: according to the one who says the פר יום הכפורים is a private offering, can a substitution take effect on it or not? What exactly is his doubt?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats רבי אלעזר's question, this time to analyze it directly rather than use it as a proof. It is setting up the next step, which will explain the basis of his doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the bull is a private offering, it seems obvious that a תמורה should take effect, since private offerings can have תמורה. So the גמרא asks what רבי אלעזר was unsure about.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself'; returning to examine a statement that was quoted earlier
He asked; raised a question that has no settled answer
What is he unsure about?

steps.confusionAlert: The text reads רבי (אליעזר) in parentheses. The correct reading, as in the Sefaria translation, is רבי אלעזר.

phrases.english: The matter itself.
Rabbi Elazar asked:
According to the one who says
the Yom Kippur bull is an individual's offering,
does it make a substitution
or does it not make a substitution?
What is his question?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the proof discussion and examines the quoted question directly
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why there is any doubt about תמורה once the bull is considered a private offering

steps.title: Do we follow the one who consecrates or the ones who receive atonement?
steps.stepSummary: The doubt is explained. The כהן גדול alone consecrated the bull with his own money, which makes it private. But it brings atonement to his fellow כהנים too, which makes it like a shared or communal offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we follow the one who consecrated it, or do we follow the ones who receive atonement through it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question by explaining the two sides of רבי אלעזר's doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If תמורה depends on the מקדיש, then the כהן גדול owns and consecrated the bull, so his תמורה works. If it depends on the מתכפר, then many כהנים get atonement, making it communal-like, so his תמורה does not work. The question is which one defines the law of תמורה.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who consecrates the animal
The one(s) who receive atonement through the offering
We go after / follow…

steps.whatToRemember: This first explanation frames רבי אלעזר's doubt as מקדיש versus מתכפר. The next step rejects this framing as obvious, and Step 6 gives the real doubt.
steps.whyThisMatters: The distinction between מקדיש and מתכפר is a basic framework that comes up across קדשים, wherever these two roles belong to different people.

phrases.english: Do we follow the one who consecrates,
or do we follow the one who receives atonement?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי בָּתַר מַקְדִּישׁ אָזְלִינַן, אִי בָּתַר מִתְכַּפֵּר אָזְלִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question raised in step 3
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The doubt is whether תמורה follows the מקדיש (the כהן גדול alone, so it works) or the מתכפר (many כהנים, so it does not work)

steps.title: Obviously the one atoned for is the one who matters
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to the way the doubt was just explained. It is obvious that we follow the person who gets atonement, as shown by a ruling of רבי יוחנן and a parallel case from תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious that we follow the one who gets atonement. As רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the one who consecrates an animal adds a fifth when redeeming it, but the one who gets atonement from it is the one who can make a תמורה with it. And similarly, one who separates תרומה from his own produce for his friend's produce has the right to choose which כהן gets it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the explanation from Step 4. The doubt cannot be about the כהן גדול paying versus the others being atoned, because the law already says we follow the one who is atoned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 said: the כהן גדול paid alone, but the bull atones for others too, so maybe it is not private. The גמרא answers that paying does not decide who can make a תמורה. רבי יוחנן ruled that the person who consecrates only has the duty of adding a חומש, while the power to make a תמורה belongs to the one who gets atonement. So the question as worded in Step 4 seems to have an obvious answer.

keyTerms.meaning: The person who gets atonement from the offering
The person who consecrates the animal, usually with his own money
Adds a fifth to the value when redeeming a consecrated item
One who separates תרומה from produce
The right to choose which כהן receives the gift

steps.confusionAlert: Two different people can be connected to one קרבן: the one who paid and consecrated it (מקדיש) and the one it atones for (מתכפר). They have different legal powers. Adding a חומש goes with the מקדיש, but making a תמורה goes with the מתכפר.

phrases.english: It is obvious that we follow the one who gets atonement,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: as Rabbi Abbahu said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
The one who consecrates adds a fifth (when redeeming),
phrases.notes: Even if he consecrated it for someone else's atonement.

phrases.english: and the one who gets atonement can make a substitution with it.
And one who separates teruma from his own produce for his friend's produce,
the right to choose which priest gets it is his!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation of the doubt given in Step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the doubt comes from the כהן גדול consecrating alone while others are atoned.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן's rule already says the power to make a תמורה follows the one who is atoned, not the one who consecrated. So who paid is irrelevant, and the doubt as stated disappears.

steps.title: The real question: are the fellow כהנים atoned as a core part or only incidentally?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that we follow the one atoned for. It reframes רבי אלעזר's doubt: are the other כהנים atoned as a fixed, essential part of the bull, or only on the side?
steps.simpleTranslation: Actually, it is obvious to him that we follow the one who gets atonement. This is what he is asking: do his fellow כהנים get atonement as a fixed part of the offering, or perhaps they get atonement only incidentally?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the objection and gives a new version of רבי אלעזר's doubt. The issue is not who paid, but how strongly the other כהנים are connected to the atonement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the fellow כהנים are atoned בקביעותא (as an essential part), they are real partners in the bull, and partners cannot make a תמורה. If they are atoned only בקופיא (incidentally), the main atonement belongs to the כהן גדול alone. Then the bull is fully his private offering, and he could make a תמורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually / in truth; used to keep the main idea while changing the explanation
His brothers the כהנים, meaning the fellow priests
In a fixed, essential way, as a core part of the offering
Incidentally, on the side, not as the main purpose

steps.whyThisMatters: This new version of the question is the one the rest of the sugya tries to answer. Everything that follows tests whether the fellow כהנים count as true partners.

phrases.english: Actually, it is obvious to him (Rabbi Elazar)
that we follow the one who gets atonement,
and this is what he is asking:
Do his fellow priests get atonement as a fixed, essential part,
or perhaps they get atonement only incidentally?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם פְּשִׁיטָא לֵיהּ דְּבָתַר מִתְכַּפֵּר אָזְלִינַן, וְהָכִי קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of Step 5 by redefining the doubt.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The doubt was about the כהן גדול paying alone versus others being atoned, which Step 5 showed has an obvious answer.
steps.terutzMaskana: The doubt is whether the fellow כהנים are atoned essentially (making them partners) or only incidentally (leaving the bull private to the כהן גדול).

steps.title: Opening a ברייתא to try to answer the question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting a ברייתא that compares the strictness of an original קרבן with the strictness of its תמורה. This quote is the setup for an attempted proof that continues next.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: There is a strictness in the original sacrifice beyond the substitute, and a strictness in the substitute beyond the original sacrifice. The strictness of the sacrifice: the sacrifice applies to an individual as well as to the community, it pushes aside שבת and טומאה, and one can make a תמורה with it. None of this is true of the substitute.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts quoting a ברייתא to try to answer רבי אלעזר's question. This is a setup step: the ברייתא continues next, and the actual proof is drawn from it there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists ways an original קרבן is more serious than a תמורה: it can belong to an individual or to the community, it overrides שבת and טומאה, and it can itself be swapped by a תמורה. The ברייתא will go on to list the ways a תמורה is stricter. The גמרא will try to use the details of this list to decide whether the כהן גדול's bull can receive a תמורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear; introduces a source brought to answer a question
A stricter law, a point of greater seriousness
The original sacrifice, as opposed to its substitute
Overrides שבת, may be offered even on שבת
Ritual impurity; some communal קרבנות may be brought even when most people are impure

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not finished here. Do not look for the conclusion of the proof yet. It comes when the ברייתא and the גמרא continue in the next lines.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
There is a strictness in the sacrifice beyond the substitute,
and a strictness in the substitute beyond the sacrifice.
The strictness of the sacrifice:
that a sacrifice applies to an individual as it does to the community,
and it overrides Shabbat and ritual impurity,
and one can make a substitution with it,
which is not so with the substitute.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to try to resolve the reframed question of Step 6.
steps.raayaObject: Whether the כהן גדול's bull can receive a תמורה, meaning whether the fellow כהנים are atoned essentially or incidentally.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא comparing the strictness of an original זבח with the strictness of its תמורה. The quote continues next.

steps.title: The ברייתא's second half: how the substitute is stricter
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its comparison. It names ways in which a תמורה is stricter than the original זבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: A substitute is stricter than the original offering in one way. Substitution takes effect even on an animal with a permanent blemish. And the substitute never goes out to non-holy status so that it could be sheared or put to work. The original offering is not like that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the ברייתא it started in the last step, now giving the other side of the comparison. This finishes the setup. The actual proof attempt comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 showed that the original offering is stricter in several ways: it can be private or communal, it overrides שבת and טומאה, and it can make a תמורה. Now we learn the opposite. Holiness 'sticks' to a תמורה even if the animal has a permanent blemish, and a תמורה can never be redeemed to become ordinary. The proof in Step 9 combines two features from Step 7: this זבח overrides שבת and טומאה, and it can make a תמורה. The strictures listed here are quoted again in Step 15.

keyTerms.meaning: A stricture; a way in which one thing is stricter than another
An animal with a permanent blemish, which can never be offered on the altar
Goes out to non-holy status, meaning it is redeemed and becomes ordinary
To be sheared and worked, the uses of an ordinary animal that are forbidden for a holy one

phrases.english: There is a stricture in the substitute beyond the offering:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהַתְּמוּרָה חָלָה עַל בַּעַל מוּם קָבוּעַ,
phrases.english: that substitution takes effect even on a permanently blemished animal,
phrases.notes: If someone tries to make a permanently blemished animal into a substitute, it still becomes fully holy.

phrases.english: and it does not go out to non-holy status
so that it could be sheared and worked
which is not so with the original offering.
phrases.notes: A blemished animal that was consecrated as an offering can be redeemed in some cases.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא that step 7 began. Step 7 gave the original offering's strictness, and this step gives the substitute's strictness.
steps.raayaObject: Whether פר יום הכפורים makes a תמורה (רבי אלעזר's question)
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא contrasting the strictures of a זבח and its תמורה

steps.title: The ברייתא must be talking about the bull
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which offering the ברייתא means. By ruling out the other options, it concludes it must be the bull. That would prove the bull makes a תמורה, because it is a קרבן יחיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: What kind of offering is this ברייתא talking about? If it is a private offering, does a private offering override שבת and טומאה? If it is a communal offering, can a communal offering make a substitute? So it must be the bull. The bull overrides שבת and טומאה because it has a fixed time. And it makes a substitute because it is a private offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns the ברייתא into a proof. It narrows down which offering fits both features, and lands on the bull.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The offering in the ברייתא must have two features: it overrides שבת and טומאה, and it can make a תמורה. Ordinary private offerings fail the first test, and communal offerings fail the second. The bull passes both: its fixed time lets it override שבת, and it counts as a קרבן יחיד, so it makes a תמורה. This would answer רבי אלעזר: the other כהנים' atonement does not make it communal.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What exactly are we talking about?
If you will say; introduces a first option to be tested
Rather, is it not...? Introduces the option the גמרא thinks is left
It has a fixed time, which is what allows an offering to override שבת and טומאה
A communal offering, which cannot make a תמורה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't get mixed up here: a 'private offering' that overrides שבת is not a contradiction. Most private offerings do not override שבת, but one with a fixed time, like the bull, does. That is exactly why the bull fits.

phrases.english: This offering, what is the case?
If you say it is an individual's offering,
does it override שבת and impurity?
Rather, if it is a communal offering,
does it make a substitute?
phrases.notes: Communal offerings cannot make a תמורה.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not the bull?
And it overrides שבת and impurity
because it has a fixed time,
and it makes a substitute
because it is an individual's offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the ברייתא quoted in steps 7–8 and draws the proof out of it.
steps.raayaObject: That פר יום הכפורים makes a תמורה, so the other כהנים' atonement is only on the side
steps.raayaSupportSource: Elimination: only the bull both overrides שבת and טומאה and can make a תמורה

steps.title: רב ששת: it could be the ram of אהרן
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת rejects the proof. The ברייתא could be talking about אילו של אהרן, the כהן גדול's ram brought as an עולה on יום כפור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: No. The ברייתא is talking about the ram of אהרן.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת shows that the proof is not forced. Another offering also fits both features of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן גדול's ram is fully his own, with no atonement for others, so it is clearly a קרבן יחיד and can make a תמורה. It also has a fixed time on יום כפור, so it overrides שבת and טומאה. Since the ram also fits the ברייתא, the proof about the bull is no longer forced. Steps 11–16 go on to debate whether the ברייתא can still be about the bull.

keyTerms.meaning: No; rejects the suggested proof
Aharon's ram, the כהן גדול's personal עולה on יום כפור (ויקרא טז:ג)

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: No,
it is talking about Aharon's ram.
phrases.notes: This is the ram brought as an עולה, which is purely private.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 9 by offering a different case the ברייתא could mean.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the ברייתא. It does not decide רבי אלעזר's question either way.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The process of elimination missed an option: the ram is also a fixed-time קרבן יחיד.

steps.title: Why the ram reading is more reasonable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports רב ששת. The ברייתא implies the substitute can be offered on a weekday. A substitute for the bull, a חטאת, is never offered: it is left to die.
steps.simpleTranslation: So too it is reasonable to say this. If you thought the ברייתא meant the bull, then it would be saying that the bull's substitute only fails to override שבת and טומאה, but on a weekday it can be offered. But it is the substitute of a חטאת, and the substitute of a חטאת is left to die!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds an argument that רב ששת's reading is the more reasonable one, since the ברייתא seems not to fit the bull. The next step challenges this argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By saying the substitute does not override שבת and טומאה, the ברייתא implies it is offered on a normal day. A bull's substitute would be a substitute of a חטאת, which is never offered and is left to die. The ram is an עולה, and the substitute of an עולה is offered as an עולה, so only the ram fits.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it is reasonable; introduces support for the view just stated
If it should enter your mind; introduces a reading in order to reject it
The substitute of a sin-offering
Goes to death; it is left to die and is not offered

steps.whatToRemember: This argument supports reading the ברייתא as the ram of אהרן, because a bull's substitute (a חטאת's substitute) is never offered. The next step rejects this support by reading 'תמורה' as the general category, which brings the bull back as a possible meaning.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a standard way the גמרא reads a source: a small hint in the wording (the substitute only fails on שבת and טומאה) tells us which case is meant.

phrases.english: So too it is reasonable,
for if it entered your mind that it means his bull,
the substitute of the bull,
is it only שבת and impurity that it does not override,
so that on a weekday it is offered?!
But it is the substitute of a sin-offering,
and the substitute of a sin-offering is left to die!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up רב ששת's rejection in step 10 with a reading of the ברייתא's wording.
steps.raayaObject: That the ברייתא refers to Aharon's ram, not the bull
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rule that the substitute of a חטאת is left to die, together with the ברייתא's implication that the substitute is offered on weekdays
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: At this point the ram reading looks stronger. Step 12 answers this by reading 'תמורה' as the general category, which keeps the bull reading alive.

steps.title: The ברייתא Could Still Be About the Bull: 'Substitute' Means Substitutes in General
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the support for רב ששת. The ברייתא may still be about the bull, and 'תמורה' there means the general category of תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Really, the ברייתא is talking about the bull. And what does 'the substitute' mean? It means the general category of substitutes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on Step 11. It says the ברייתא can still be about the bull.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 argued that a substitute for the bull is never offered, so the ברייתא cannot mean the bull. The answer here is that 'תמורה' in the ברייתא does not mean the bull's own substitute. It means תמורה as a general concept, so the line about being offered on a weekday is about substitutes in general.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / in truth (used to keep the original position)
The general category or 'name' of תמורה, not one specific substitute
His bull: the כהן גדול's bull on יום כפור

steps.confusionAlert: 'שם תמורה' does not mean 'the name of the substitute animal.' It means 'תמורה as a general category.' The ברייתא's comparison is still about the bull, but the word 'תמורה' is read broadly.

phrases.english: No, really it is his bull.
phrases.notes: Returns to the proof of Step 9.

phrases.english: And what is meant by 'substitute'?
The general category of substitute.
phrases.notes: Not the bull's own substitute, which would die.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the support for רב ששת given in Step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the support from 'offered on a weekday' that was brought for רב ששת's reading.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumed 'תמורה' means the bull's own substitute. It can mean תמורה in general.

steps.title: Then Maybe 'Offering' Also Means Offerings in General?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this: if 'תמורה' means the general category, then maybe 'זבח' also means offerings in general.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then 'offering' should also mean the general category of offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges Step 12. If one word in the ברייתא is read as a general category, why not the other word too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'זבח' also means offerings in general, the ברייתא is not about any particular offering. Then it says nothing about the bull, and the proof from Step 9 falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
The general category of offerings

phrases.english: If so,
then 'offering' should also mean the general category of offerings?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, זֶבַח נָמֵי — שֵׁם זֶבַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading in Step 12 by applying the same logic to 'זבח'.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 12's reading of 'תמורה' as a general category
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'תמורה' is general, 'זבח' should be general too. Then the ברייתא would not be about the bull at all.

steps.title: No, the ברייתא Does Not Mean Offerings in General
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is not teaching about the general category of offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא is not teaching about the general category of offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. 'זבח' in the ברייתא means a specific offering, not offerings in general.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So the two words are read differently. 'תמורה' can be general, but 'זבח' must be one specific offering. That keeps the bull as a possible meaning. The proof for this answer comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: It does not teach / it is not talking about

phrases.english: It is not teaching about the general category of offerings.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes how the two words in the ברייתא are read.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both 'זבח' and 'תמורה' should be read as general categories.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only 'תמורה' is general. 'זבח' refers to a specific offering.

steps.title: Proof from the Strictures the ברייתא Lists for a Substitute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins proving its answer. It quotes the ברייתא's strictures of תמורה: it takes effect on a permanently blemished animal, and it never becomes ordinary to be sheared or worked.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this? From what the ברייתא teaches: a substitute is stricter, because a substitute takes effect even on an animal with a permanent blemish, and it does not become ordinary (חולין) so that it could be sheared or used for work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how we know 'זבח' is not general. It starts answering by quoting the strictures the ברייתא listed for a תמורה. This quote sets up the argument in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, if someone sanctifies an animal with a permanent blemish, it gets only money-holiness and can be redeemed to become ordinary. A תמורה is stricter: it takes hold fully even on such an animal, and it can never be redeemed to be sheared or worked. The גמרא will use these strictures to show that 'זבח' cannot mean all offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know?
An animal with a permanent blemish
Becomes ordinary, non-holy
To be sheared and to be worked

phrases.english: From where do we know?
From what it teaches:
A stricture in the substitute:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהַתְּמוּרָה חָלָה עַל בַּעַל מוּם קָבוּעַ,
phrases.english: that the substitute takes effect on a permanently blemished animal,
and it does not go out to ordinary status
to be sheared and to be worked.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts proving the answer in Step 14 by quoting part of the ברייתא from Step 8.
steps.raayaObject: That 'זבח' in the ברייתא is a specific offering, not offerings in general.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's list of strictures of תמורה over the original זבח.

steps.title: If 'Offering' Were General, Some Offering Already Has These Strictures
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that if 'זבח' meant offerings in general, the strictures could not be unique to תמורה, because some offering already has them. The example comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you think that 'offering' means the general category of offerings, there is an offering that also has these rules.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the logic of its proof, but the sentence continues on the next amud. It is setting up to name an offering that already has these strict rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says these rules make תמורה stricter than the זבח. If 'זבח' meant all offerings, that would be false, because some offerings already follow these same rules. So 'זבח' must mean one specific offering that lacks them, such as the bull.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it would enter your mind (if you were to think)
But there is (introduces a counterexample)

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind:
that 'offering' means the general category of offerings,
but there is...
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud, which names the offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ: מַאי זֶבַח — שֵׁם זֶבַח, וְהָא אִיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the strictures quoted in Step 15 to argue against reading 'זבח' as general.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The existence of an offering that already shares these strictures (named on the next amud).
